fact: The General Directorate of National Land Domain announced on 11 January 2026 the nationwide rollout of the AMLAK information system to gradually replace the paper land title booklet with an electronic title, with all cadastral and land registry offices to be connected ultimately.

Executive decree 26-15 of 7 January 2026 instituted the electronic land booklet, and the Direction generale du Domaine national announced Amlak would be generalised to all cadastre and land conservation directorates in preparation for issuing it.
The director general says all national cadastral plans and the land conservation archives are digitised, with over 27 million documents in a database and over 14 million properties digitised.
The director general says the database covers 217 land conservations across the country.

The director general says the Fada El Djazair portal, launched May 2024, gives access to cadastral and land information and offers over 6,500 electronic services, plus electronic payment of land service fees.
Algeria's finance minister said on 12 December 2024 that the land file and archives of the land conservation offices have been digitised, covering property status, real rights and owners.

La Sentinelle reports that in Guelma wilaya the land conservations are digitising property records (94% at Bouchegouf, 80% at two others, about 60% in Guelma town), rural cadastre is complete and urban cadastre about 98%, and the sector now has a land database.

La Sentinelle reports the national platform Fada El Djazair is accessible to citizens and public bodies to consult cadastral plans and request documents remotely, with a further tool, Amlak, still to come.
Algérie360 reports that the DGDN's Fadaeldjazair portal runs on a unified central database holding over 27 million documents from 217 land conservations and over 14 million digitised properties.

The DGDN's Fadaeldjazair portal lets users request the land booklet, negative certificate, deed copies and cadastral extracts online, pay by Edahabia or CIB card via SATIM and track the request; some formalities still need an office visit.

The Direction generale du Domaine national announced on 11 January 2026 the generalisation of the Amlak information system, a unified national system with a central database integrating the cadastre, land conservation and State Domains, with immediate response to requests at cadastre and land conservation counters.
The Direction generale du Domaine national said Amlak was generalised to all directorates of the cadastre, land conservation and State Domains.
The Director General of State Domains called in April 2026 for full use of the Amlak information system in State property, cadastre and land conservation activities.
A pilot was launched at the Dar El Beida and El Harrach land conservation offices to issue cadastral and land registry extracts through the national digital services portal.
Algérie Zoom reports the Direction Générale du Domaine National generalised the Amlak system, with a central national database for cadastre and land conservation, on 11 January 2026.
Algérie Zoom reports the generalisation of Amlak covers all local directions of cadastre, land conservation and state property, without exception.
APS quotes the portal head saying the Ministry of Finance's Fada El Djazair geoportal, launched March 2024, serves cadastral and land data.
APS says the geoportal carries cadastral and land data for the whole national territory.
APS says users download cadastral and land documents on the portal without visiting the land registry office, cutting delivery from a month to eight days.

Minister Faid said the State Domains services have a dedicated land and State property information system to digitise cadastre, land conservation and State property activities, and that integration and digitisation systems were launched for the cadastre and land conservation directorates.
system: Land and State property information system
